Sentence: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance.
Content: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance. No issues with snapping or breaking at all.I still have nitpicks about the color range (lack of oranges and yellows, mostly) but have found that, while they're still wet, they do mix quite nicely. You can achieve a lot of good in-between colors by mixing on the surface you're creating on before the marks dry.Though I am still so sure I will run out of white and yellow before anything else, which has me wishing I could buy individuals.Despite that, these are one of my favorite sets of art supplies in recent years. I'm obsessed.Updated pros/consPROS:-Surprisingly opaque-very saturated colors-dries fast and layers well (colors do dry a bit darker, as it goes with acrylic)-The brush tip is actually the best, no more pumping a paint markerCONS:-color range is lacking a bit in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case takes up a lot of space when opened--------------------------------original review--------------------------------(I got these today, so this is a 'first impressions' review)I'm a artist and art instructor by trade, and I like to use a wide variety of materials to make recommendations to students as well as find new supplies for myself.These markers are pretty solid- I like acrylic paint for its opaque layering properties, as well as the quick dry, and these markers are pretty effective at both. As with acrylic paint, you do have some transparency and a need to layer, especially on lighter colors like white and yellow, or on top of darker colors. But overall, the coverage is pretty solid and the saturation is impressive.The case is a bit weird, you have to be careful separating the layers (they tuck into these little ridges at the back to hold together, and I can see there being a risk of snapping) but otherwise it seems convenient.The color range is odd. Acrylic dries darker than it applies, so after you let them sit for a moment you do have deeper hues, but the black included is SO much darker than the deepest of any other color.I'd really love to see a deep jewel tone range for each hue so I can achieve solid depth without just resorting to black. A deep alizarin crimson, phthalo blue or Paynes grey, deep viridian- the problem, I assume, is that these markers all have an almost chalky binder to keep the opacity up, and it sacrifices the deeper values as a result (many of the above listed colors are traditionally transparent.) So I'm not sure this would even be possible with the current pigment/binders used.Still, it would be wonderful to have a really deep set of colors, and if I'm just missing them in this 60 pack, I'd love to be directed to where I can grab them.Also, there's not a lot of orange options, and there are a whole lot of certain other colors, like green and pink.Anyway tldr;PROS:-nice opacity-very Saturated-dries fast and layers well-smooth flow with convenient brush tipCONS:-color range is lacking in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case is a bit confusingI'll come back after a couple months of use to update on whether the markers have any trouble or not, but as of today I'm liking them.

Sentence: I don’t ever color on black paper so it’s not an issue to me but that might be a problem covering black lines in coloring books.
Content: These were really nice paint pens. The things that kept me from giving it five stars were as follows: the case is kind of a pain to deal with. You have to unsnap each layer and lay them all out to have easy access to any color. And then when putting the cases back together you have to make sure that the clip on the case above doesn’t get snapped in when you clip the one below. It just seems very unnecessary when a zipper case that you can unfold and lay out works much better. I have another set of 60 of these almost identical pens and they came in a zipper case that was much easier to deal with. I will say that the case looks very nice tho. My second problem that I took a star off for is that some caps fit nicely in the back of the pen when using it while others were too loose and wouldn’t stay on. Sentence: These pens are also great for card-making and stencils.
Content: This 24-piece acrylic paint pen kit is a blast--and at a little over $1 a pen, it gives you a lot of entertainment hours for your buck!The set comes in a beautifully decorated hardcover case, with the name "Ohuhu" (leaf in the 'O'), and drawings of leaves, flowers, stars, cactus, a cute gecko, peaceful dove, and other geometrics, designed to inspire, printed on the front in white. The back has Ohuhu's motto, "Draw. Feel. Empower." and a bunch of legal data printed on it. The zipper on the case moves very smoothly, and each pen has its own velcro loop to hold it secure in travel. This would make a perfect Plein Air sketch set, so light and easy to use.Inside, there is a multilingual instruction booklet and 3 swatch cards. 1 swatch card is filled out and has a white background, and there are also two blanks: one white and one black. I encourage you to fill both of these out, first, to prime your pens and get them ready to do an art, and second, so you can notice how the different background colors affect the perceived color of the pens. Even though you are using the exact same color on both cards, the final outcome looks VERY different. After that, you're ready to go!The colors of the paint are opaque, provided you let the bottom colors dry before adding more on top. This takes maybe a minute. You can also blend the colors just a bit by working two colors together quickly, but be careful that you don't foul and muddy your pen tips.Protip: if you've treated your item with gesso (highly recommended), you can blend, work, and even dilute the colors with a damp brush and a little water, allowing you to create watercolor-like effects or blend and smooth sharp lines. The gesso protects your item from the water and smooths the surface in order to accept the paint more readily. It's fairly cheap and available here on Amazon. Think of it as primer, except for art!These pens may not be as versatile as a full acrylic paint set, but neither are they as expensive or as messy. For a more advanced artist, these pens make a great color sketch set so you can get ideas down in the books quickly and conveniently, then you can use your full acrylic or oil paint set to make a full final copy. These paints are great for casual artists or smaller multimedia art projects such as rock painting or just adding a few quick touches to a knitting or sewing project. Not everybody wants or needs to bother with a full paint kit. These pens are also great for card-making and stencils. I'm sure there's a ton of other uses I've forgotten, or don't have the wit to imagine. 10/10, versatile, affordable, and FUN.

Content: I’m not an artist, but we keep some art supplies around for my daughter’s school projects. We tried these out on a coloring page and were pleased with the results. I let it dry and then left it out in a torrential downpour for three days and even when I rubbed it with a dry paper towel, it was mostly intact. Sharpies do not hold up at all on these metal tags, so now we have a way to use these tags up. Overall, these seem to be quality markers and when these are eventually used up or dry out, we will likely replace them and keep a set around.

Content: For paint markers these Sharpies are quite smooth. On a mixed media paper, the markers laid down nice opaque lines. Content: I got these markers for writing on rocks mainly and they are good for that. Sentence: I do purchase good quality coloring books and this does not happen with the regular sharpie markers.
Content: I like to use sharpie markers to color so I definitely wanted to try these. I purchased the 12 earth tones with a bullet tip and the 12 pop with the brush tip and have mixed feelings. Sentence: This would be great for adult coloring books as well.
Content: These Sharpie earth tone acrylic markers are fantastic! The colors are gorgeous and different than the usual Sharpie colors. Sentence: it looks great on black paper.
Content: These are pricey for acrylic markers, but I guess you’re paying for the Sharpie brand name. The ink flows well and has good coverage; it looks great on black paper. I think the tips are pretty good quality. Just be aware that you’re buying 12 brush tip markers and 12 bullet tip markers, not 24 markers with dual tips — which I think was sort of an odd choice. The brush tips and bullet tips come in different colors, which is kinda weird to me but I’m glad to have 24 colors as opposed to just 12 repeated twice. Some of the colors are fairly similar to each other, which isn’t ideal to me with a set of 24. Overall, while these are perfectly serviceable markers I don’t feel the brand name makes them worth the price when you can easily find much larger sets of other brands for cheaper.

Sentence: The water-based acrylic ink flows smoothly, and the colors are vibrant and opaque, even on dark paper.
Content:
I love that this set comes with different tip sizes, so I can experiment with fine details and bold strokes. The water-based acrylic ink flows smoothly, and the colors are vibrant and opaque, even on dark paper. I’ve tried them on paper, canvas, and even wood, and they worked great on all surfaces.

One thing to note is that some colors take a couple of layers to be fully opaque, but that’s expected with water-based markers. Also, shaking and priming the pens before use is necessary, but once you get the hang of it, it’s easy.

Overall, this is a fantastic set for beginners like me who want to explore acrylic markers without spending too much. I highly recommend them for anyone getting into painting or mixed media!

Content: I can’t believe how well these pens write for the value. There is a wide variety of colors. I was hesitant to buy them because I thought they would be poor quality for the price but I was pleasantly surprised. I use them in my art journal and layer them with paints. They work perfectly.

Sentence: I was testing out some new stamps designs today to see how they worked for some stamped flowers and some animals.
Content:
I have a lot of acrylic markers/pens and it would seem like I wouldn't need yet another set, however, so much depends on their tips as to how well they work for what you are using them for. I like these dot tips in two sizes. The markers come with a color chart on the back of the box. The problem is, the markers are not numbered nor are their colors printed on them. This makes it difficult to know exactly which marker you are using. I have been using them the last couple of days. I made a Christmas tree just using dots in different colors of green for the branches, browns for the trunk, a gold star at the top and red lights. It was fun making it. I was testing out some new stamps designs today to see how they worked for some stamped flowers and some animals. At times I used the tip not to make dots but finer lines to color the stamps in. Some of the flowers I colored in and a few of the other designs showed through to the other side of the paper. I colored the rather large tree in my sketch book and had no bleed threw. I enjoyed using these markers, but it would be nice to be able to identify each color marker easily.

I appreciate the opportunity to try these markers. Thank you.

Sentence: Also, I would use a thicker paper or adult coloring book with a paper separating any other drawings, as they do bleed through a bit.

Sentence: I'm normally a brand snob, enjoying only the finest of my curated art tools and wanting nothing but the best for what I create in my sketchbook.
Content:
I'm normally a brand snob, enjoying only the finest of my curated art tools and wanting nothing but the best for what I create in my sketchbook. However, even though I hadn't heard of this brand before, I was really surprised by the quality of their markers. Compared to POSCA and Arrtx, these are closer to POSCA in terms of vibrancy. They pop off the page, plus they went on very smooth and opaque. Only one of the colors required a little touch up in my swatch book to get full coverage.

One huge selling point (and a gripe I have about most brands of markers/pens) is that these markers are labeled/numbered on both ends. Again, this is huge. I never understood why Arrtx made you put stickers on their paint markers and try to eyeball which sticker went with which color. I very much appreciated Betem's simple design here and the ease of use to quickly identify what each color is, whether the marker is up or down.

I have read that others are totally frustrated by the fact that these paint brush-pens are not labeled and there is no semblance of order in the numbering.  But if you look at the colors on the outside top of the pen you have a pretty good idea of the hue and can experiment with the color. This works perfectly well for me and happy with these.  I like the fact that the paint  dries appropriately fast allowing for layering without having to wait any length of time. Sentence: I noted how consistently the ink flowed the instant I opened the black fineliner and drew a delicate vine over river stone.
Content: I noted how consistently the ink flowed the instant I opened the black fineliner and drew a delicate vine over river stone. There was no spatter at the beginning, and there was no unexpected fade midway through a curve. Simply giving the tip a little shake was all that was required to prime it, and after that, the line density remained consistent throughout the whole process. During the process of filling the petals, the accompanying dot tip came into action; a small touch resulted in precise polka dots, while a heavier press resulted in significant circles that were ideal for the centers. Changing the tips of your pencil in the middle of a stroke is as natural as switching between different grades of pencil, but there is no need to roll around the table looking for a third pen. It would seem like a little spread to have twenty-four different hues, but when it is stacked, it really amounts to hundreds of different tones. After letting the first layer dry completely before applying the second coat, I painted the jar lantern with a combination of teal and pastel yellow on day two. As a result of each layer sitting on top of the previous one without blending into the mud, the gradients were clear and produced a pleasant glow when a tea light flickered within. This demonstrates that the pigmentation is robust enough to stand on its own rather than only serving as accents, since even the lighter colors, which are often weaker in other markers, covered the black glass with confidence.

All 72 colors have both the fine and brush nibs (one on each side of the pen) with a cap to keep them fresh, and make putting pen to paper and other media a smooth, flowing experience that leaves behind an opaque color that is fun to make and joyful to see.  The colors are just beautiful!  There are also 2 metallic colors to add shining gold or silver highlights where you want them.  I will be using these pens to embellish hand made cards, note pads and envelopes, and I am sure there will be other applications that arise as well.  These pens really make you want to create something unique that is colorful and beautiful, and I plan to use them to do just that over and over again.

They come in a nice case with a zipper to keep all the pens together and protect them.  Each pen has an elastic holder to keep it in place and to keep the set organized.  Mine did not have a color chart which some reviewers have referenced, but I don’t really need that.  The case and the pens themselves display the colors admirably.  I love these pens and highly recommend.

Sentence: Perfect for seasonal window art, mirror messages, mason jar labels, handmade gifts, greeting cards, and crafts.
Content:
Beautiful palette of rich, gorgeous paint markers. What’s a paint marker? I had no clue, but the vivid colors and multimedia options made this set irresistible. They feel like markers but deliver the impact of paint: not messy, just richer and more saturated, with precise application.
The double-tip pens give you options, fine or bold, and every color I tried was vibrant and beautiful. Yes, they work on glass! Perfect for seasonal window art, mirror messages, mason jar labels, handmade gifts, greeting cards, and crafts. The glass application can be removed with a stiff brush, fingernail, or dish soap.
I tested them on foil (hello, freezer meals!), fabric (school/camp labeling), and even Halloween pumpkins. Smooth cotton worked great; textured fabric was less precise but still held up through the washer and dryer.
On smooth surfaces, you can wipe away while still moist, no mess. Once dry, it can be scraped off or removed with solvent. Porous surfaces like fabric are more permanent, so use with care. Kids can absolutely use this if supervised and wearing art clothes or coverups.
For cleanup: Dawn dish soap and Goo Gone both worked. Hand soap removed it from skin easily. The only lasting stains were on porous surfaces like fabric and paper. For more permanent crafts on smooth surfaces, a topcoat might help seal your designs.
This set is exactly what you need to create all your art, all purpose, from practical to creative, from freezer meals to wearable crafts, from wall art and graphic designs to custom tees and woodcraft. One set, endless possibilities.

Sentence: Once fully dried, the acrylic has the best staying-power on matte surfaces without using a fixative.
Content:
Since I enjoy all kinds of crafts and have crafty kids, I was excited to try this set of acrylic markers from Artecho. To summarize, I think it is a decent value for mixed-media use, especially for use with kids. However, a lack of quality control and many similar colors may not satisfy an adult artist.

Pros: I have used many types of non-toxic and paint markers in the past on a variety of mediums, and was thrilled to receive 72 colors in this set. The brush heads are smooth and a delight to work with. The fine tips most resemble traditional press-down paint marker tips, though you don't have to press these down to work - a real improvement! The rainbow of colors is very attractive in the protective, easy-to-transport case. All markers can be easily accessed when the case is open.

Now for the drawbacks. Some of the paints look best on shiny surfaces, but tend to rub off when touched, even after drying. Once fully dried, the acrylic has the best staying-power on matte surfaces without using a fixative. Some of the colors are really beautiful and smooth ("carmine", "sapphire"). Others are weakly pigmented or look muddy ("watermelon", "emerald"). The weak pigments don’t cover darker surfaces or lines, so beware if you’re trying to layer. I was super disappointed at the noticeable difference between the color of the brush and fine tip on many of the markers. See the picture of the color chart: the upper half of each box is the brush side, and the lower half of the box is the fine tip. In most cases, the brush color was quite a bit more pigmented and vibrant than the fine tip color. This difference means I cannot switch between tip types and expect my work to look consistent.

The numbering system and color names seem illogical, and the markers are not organized in the case according to either the numbering or the color chart. Many of the names inadequately reflect the actual color; for example, "brown" is a light pink, and "indigo" is a greenish gray. "Blackberry" and "crimson" are both pale pink. In fact, 18 of the markers are pink tones, including "beige", "camel", and "earth red", and similar in appearance. As the paints are not true to the color of their lids, it is hard to find particular shades unless you rearrange them and use a color chart. However, the included chart lists 120 colors, and there are only 72 in this set, leaving many blank boxes. The color chart is also printed on shiny paper, so the colors tend to smear.

Overall, I think the value of this introductory set is fine at its current price point (24 u.s.d. at the time of review). The markers will be good for painting on stones, wood, and other mixed media crafts with kids (especially kids who like pink), and I think they'll hold up through multiple projects. However, if you're a serious artist or looking to add to your existing stock of acrylic markers, I don't recommend this set from Artecho.

Content:

Sentence: I love the Artecho set because right off the bat, it comes in a professional, standard black artist's zipping carrying case.
Content:
There are so many brands to choose from now days when choosing an Acrylic Marker Set. But there is something to be said for a HIGH QUALITY set, backed by a profession company tailored to art.

I love the Artecho set because right off the bat, it comes in a professional, standard black artist's zipping carrying case. Slots to fit 72 markers with ease. There is a center fold out portion so it's compact. Each marker is specially numbered, & with the set comes a color card indicator. This is where each color is identified by number & the artist is able to color in a small square for reference.

These are dual tip markers- Fine Tip, & Brush Tip. Generally, me personally, when I use them, I start with my Fine Tip for either outlining, or beginning a design then fill in with Brush Tip.

These are decadent pens! Rich colours that provide a lot of ink flow. I have another set by another company, & the quality is sub- par in comparison. You do not have to shake these, or worry about ink bleeds, or pressing down too hard to get ink out. Simply Colour/ create your design with ease as if you were using a colored pencil. These really do give matte finish acrylic pigment. They blend well with eachother too. I have used them on canvas and a hard cardstock colouring book & truly this is real high quality acrylic ink.

I was waiting for the perfect set, and when this fell in my lap i couldn't have been more delighted. Its an absolute 5 star for professional artists, intermediate & beginners, all. Great for trips as it's already got a convenient case. easy to pack on the daily in a handbag or backpack, as it measures roughly 13" long & 7" wide 2-3" deep.

It a remarkable find, and others stands out above the other acrylic pen set by far!

Content:
These markers come with a fancy carrying case that disassembles to display all of the markers for use and then snaps back together for transport. It also comes with a few projects to start with - paint by number pictures and a couple of wooden ornaments - as well as comprehensive tutorials for blending colors and more.

It’s very good to have swatch pages in both black and white and these markers work well on wood, rock, glass and more.

That being said, the points of the brush tips were a little bit soft and at times the one-coat coverage could have been better. Not suitable for writing letters or details; better to get fine point or felt tip markers for that.

Sentence: I do like the pen holder.
Content:
This is a very nice set of acrylic markers. There are 36 markers with a brush tip that by the pressure you use when using them you will get thin to fat lines. You can also make dots with the tips of the pens. I was able to swatch out all the colors in my swatch book and on the included white and black swatch papers. You also get some other items to color which I haven't done yet. I only had trouble with one pen, B88, where I could not get the cap off even with gripping it with a silicon gripper. I finally had to ask my husband to see if he could remove the cap and with some big effort, he was able to. When I looked closely at the pen once the cap was off, it was evident that there had been a ink leak that had dried and basically glued the cap on.

I do like the assortment of colors. I like how they swatched in my book and the white swatch card that came with the pens. The black swatch card the colors seemed to be streaky with the coverage not being very good. I do like the pen holder. It is easy to open each tray and to put them back. The colors come out opaque. You get a silver and a gold pen as well as black and white.

I do appreciate the opportunity to try out these pens. Thank you

Sentence: Adherence to paper and canvas is quite good, but the dried paint can easily be scraped off of coated surfaces, so the recommendation by the manufacturer to utilize a clear top coat is a wise one.
Content: This is a very nice set of 168 acrylic paint pens, offering a nice color palette.  The paint flows very smoothly, and has good coverage. The tips are suitable for a wide variety of painting styles, including calligraphy. Adherence to paper and canvas is quite good, but the dried paint can easily be scraped off of coated surfaces, so the recommendation by the manufacturer to utilize a clear top coat is a wise one. Given how easily the paint can be scraped, I'm skeptical about the longevity on plastic or glass.The set does come with a few replacement nibs, should you need them.  I'll note that one of the pens was dried out, with both the nib and the internal wick clogged with dried acrylic paint, and it could not be salvaged. It's possible that the cap wasn't fully sealed during shipment.At the price per pen, I wouldn't expect professional quality, so I'm satisfied.

Sentence: The metallic colors are absolutely gorgeous—vibrant, shiny, and they really pop, especially on black paper and dark surfaces.
Content:
I’m so impressed with this 12-pack of metallic markers! Each pen has a dual tip—one end is a flexible brush tip that really feels like using a paintbrush, and the other is a finer point that's great for more detailed work. Both tips are loaded with rich, highly pigmented ink that glides on smoothly.

The metallic colors are absolutely gorgeous—vibrant, shiny, and they really pop, especially on black paper and dark surfaces.

I originally bought these for making Halloween props (which they’re perfect for), but there are so many ways to use them—scrapbooking, card-making, labeling, you name it. The quick-dry, alcohol-based ink helps prevent smudging, which is a big plus for detailed crafting.

Overall, these are high-quality, fun to use, and super versatile. Highly recommend for any DIYer or artist looking to add some metallic flair to their work!

Sentence: I have tested them on wood, rocks, watercolor paper and black drawing.
Content: This 12 pack of dual tip metallic markers are very pretty with a good variety of shades to choose from. They are not as vibrant as the images show; I have tested them on wood, rocks, watercolor paper and black drawing. The ink/paint flows smoothly from both the fine and brush tips on all tested surfaces and there was no bleed through on either type of paper even with two coats. One coat was enough for my wooden coasters and rock projects; however, I used two coats on some spots on the coasters for a deeper color. Some of the colors definitely look more metallic than others and the colors on the back of the box do not match the actual markers making it was difficult to distinguish some of them; names of colors on the pens would have been more helpful. I colored over the chart on the back with each marker so that I could see the difference; red and rose red are confusing me still. I love the colors regardless and these are a nice addition to my growing collection of paint pens. I would absolutely recommend these and $8.99 is a great price for this 12 pack though I’d personally have chosen the 24 pack if it had been offered to me and would be more likely to purchase that for its $14.99 price tag.

Sentence: Haiducul likes to take notes on black paper.
Content:
Mrs. Haiducul likes to take notes on black paper. To each their own, I say. But it does mean that she is always on the lookout for pens that will stand out on black. She was so impressed with these, that they immediately replaced the set she had been working with. She found the colors to be nicely vibrant, the pen nibs to be good for controlled lines and wider coverage, and that there was, in fact, a noticeable metallic sheen to the colors.

Only time will tell as to whether they dry out too quickly or the nibs wear too fast, and if either of those things become evident I will jump back in here and update, but after a week of use, these are quite nice with no discernible issues. And for $8 bucks? That makes these a really good value, as well.

So yeah, these were a hit and get a full five stars.

The brush tips are very nice.
Content:
This set of acrylic markers has exceeded my expectations. They are easy to use (no priming, no shaking, just uncap and get to creating!), and they write beautifully. They would be awesome for general painting applications on pretty much any surface but would also function very nicely for hand lettering.
They dry quickly - but not instantly, so be careful not to smudge them. Wait a few seconds, though and after that they stay put.
The color range of these markers is really interesting. They're all vibrant and well-pigmented, and there is a range of both standard bright shades, a few fluorescents, and even a really nice range of Morandi-style muted tones that are just gorgeous. There are also a gold and silver metallic that shine so nicely!
They generally provide good coverage, though some of the paler shades are a lot more translucent than I'd like (but it seems that's a problem across almost every brand, save a few. I put down some black and then tried the white over the top and it was not opaque at all. Aside from maybe 4 or 5 of the palest shades though, most of these markers will likely work well on black paper and other darker surfaces.
The brush tips are very nice. They're not all exactly consistent in firmness or in juiciness, but none of them were dry and all of them are quite functional (just some are juicier than others).
I'm concerned a bit about how long these will last since each pen contains two different colors, so the capacity for each color may be less than you would find in a single-color pen, but time will tell!
I look forward to trying their single-color acrylic markers soon, too. These rival most of the other brands that I own, and I can't say enough good things about not having to prime and shake before use.

Sentence: Not only can I use this for painting, I can use this for nail art, canvas, thick paper, stone and possibly unglazed ceramics.
Content: This is such a good set of acrylic markers! This is my second product from this company and they haven’t disappointed me yet. I have been into watercolor recently as a form of therapy. The colors are very vivid and the felt tips are sturdy and won’t easily fall apart or fray. It is quick drying and could be used for so many projects. Not only can I use this for painting, I can use this for nail art, canvas, thick paper, stone and possibly unglazed ceramics. Content:
I have the smaller 36 pack of dual Grabie markers, so when I saw they had come out with a larger pack, I grabbed them up.:)

They are the same size and quality as the smaller pack, although the coloring on the marker packaging is different (relief). They also seem to have gone through a color name and number change for some of the colors that were included in the 36; you'll find most of the 36 pack here (with some that look slightly different). This pack covers a wide variety of colors, and there weren't really any (for this coloring anyways) that I was wishing were included.

I absolutely love that these don't have to be primed, and they have brush tips instead of hard nibs. The downside is that if you aren't careful (and honestly, even if you are), the tips of the brushes can break down farely quickly, which makes more detailed work very hard. They can also get bits of dried paint on them, so be prepared to pick the little bits off.
As of writing this, I don't think Grabie offers replacement tips, but I believe they are pretty similar to another brands brush tips, that you can buy replacements for, fairly cheap.

The really lovely thing about these is that they don't bleed through (like some acrylics have separation liquid that leaks through). You can easily color a double sided page, and have zero issues come through the back (given your paper quality, super thin types might show through, I'm unsure).

There's mutliple ways to use these; on rocks, glass paper, vinyl, plastic, etc (given you have a sealant) and I'm still finding extra uses for them, like adding details to coloring pages, or fixing some art when I've gone outside the lines with the medium I'm using, or even to bring back the original color on clay that's darkened too much.

They're very opaque, so you do need to be careful when coloring in pages; you'll want to have a fineliner ready to go over lines if you color over, as these will either soften the lines, or completely wipe them out. You need to be slow while coloring portions in, because if you are fast, you'll get streaks or blotches in the paint (like some areas of my coloring page; book is A Million Kittens). Do make sure to shake them prior to using to blend them.

My main gripe is that they really downgraded on the carry case packaging. I love the 36 pack case; it's softer plastic and textured, with no sharp edges, and it's easy to pull the markers out (and put them back).
With this larger pack, the packaging is a thicker, cheaper plastic that I can't get the markers out, or put them away, without scraping my hands up from the sharp opening. It can be frustrating. I really wish they'd stayed with the same packaging.

I do really like these and they've gone into my travel art bag. My original pack has yet to run out of ink, so they seem like they last a good bit. I'll have to report back if/when they do.

Sentence: Plan to use a sealant or similar to protect your paintings done with these markers.
Content: I love paint markers. I'm not sure there's an entirely logical process here... I don't use them anywhere near as much as I should given how many I've gotten, but I identified as an artist in my youth, and having fun art supplies readily available is a lot like breathing fresh air for me.I have ordered at least a half dozen paint marker packs through Vine, including several other sets from GuangNa. Generally, they earn 4 stars from me. I have been very frustrated by their lack of true green shades in their other sets. This set covers it. Wow, does it cover it.Some things you should know if you get this: Numbers are in the 600s, 700s, and 800s. For numbers that could be easily confused, they put a small dot in the upper left to indicate the top of the number. I show this in my video.For filling in your own color card, the row closest to it was almost entirely the left side, and you gradually move right as you go through each row. There are exceptions, but this helped me save time searching for the correct square once I realized.You may note the colors are not exact matches of the printed colors in many cases. I don't know why they don't make a color card and take a picture of it, but this discrepancy has been very normal with already primed paint markers.These acrylic paint markers come primed. You do not need to shake/press to prepare them for use, and these are much easier to control than the kinds that require priming. However, these are also more matte in appearance when dried and relatively easy to scratch. Plan to use a sealant or similar to protect your paintings done with these markers. It's a question of trade-offs. I prefer the ease of use these provide even knowing more work is necessary to protect my creations. You may not.Regardless, I'm thrilled with the color selection of these markers. I can't wait to do more with them!

Sentence: They play nicely with uv resin, colored pencil, microns and sharpies.The amount of money you pay for the variety and quality of ink is stunning.
Content: I think I actually got these from Amazon Vine so I didn't pay for them initially, but I'm about to buy them again. I purchased them in December 2024 and I'm writing this review in December 2025, and I've used these for a bunch of projects so far.The paint is buildable, and some of the lighter colors can be sheer on dark backgrounds, but given enough time, they do build up to become opaque. They play nicely with uv resin, colored pencil, microns and sharpies.The amount of money you pay for the variety and quality of ink is stunning. The pictures I've attached are both pieces I've done for my clients.

Sentence: They also work well on watercolor paper, and I’ll be using them for mixed media art too.
Content: This was my first time using markers on 3D prints, and they worked great. The color went on smooth and even with no streaks or clumps. I used them on a Santa and Rudolph I printed for Christmas, and they turned out way better than I expected. The only thing I didn’t like was the printing on the caps—it’s either too faint or too close in color to see easily, so I ended up labeling the barrels myself. They also work well on watercolor paper, and I’ll be using them for mixed media art too. None of my markers came dried out. They were all juicy and ready to go.

Sentence: The paint is opaque and dries fast, making it great for layering but not for blending.The set includes a small sketchbook with about 20 thick cardstock pages in white, gray, purple, and black, plus two swatch sheets.I do like paint pens, but I got these mostly for my kids.
Content: This is a nice set of fine tip acrylic markers with a good range of colors. The pens are a little hard. On a fresh pen you can see the paint slowly saturating the tip and one side usually fills faster. The pens work well once started and lay down consistent, clean lines. The firm tips feel durable but wear down with heavy use. My 10 year old used the black for outlining and the tip widened from 0.7 mm to about 2 mm, though it still works fine. The paint is opaque and dries fast, making it great for layering but not for blending.The set includes a small sketchbook with about 20 thick cardstock pages in white, gray, purple, and black, plus two swatch sheets.I do like paint pens, but I got these mostly for my kids. They were super excited and love them. Overall it feels worth the price and works nicely for arts and crafts.

Sentence: I’ve used them to label notebooks, on page tabs where I wanted a little color, on the office coffee Keurig, on plastic cups, on rocks, and on regular paper and coloring books.They dry relatively fast, however, they are not for layering.
Content: These are acrylic paint pens with a variety of applications.I’ve used these for so many things. I’ve used them to label notebooks, on page tabs where I wanted a little color, on the office coffee Keurig, on plastic cups, on rocks, and on regular paper and coloring books.They dry relatively fast, however, they are not for layering. You get an opaque finish with one coat on both non/porous and porous surfaces, but you really can’t go over it again with the same color or another color. It will pull the original layer off on non-porous and it will soak right through on porous.I still like them. They give a nice fine point for exact application and bright colors for your crafts.

Sentence: Pens work great and the included book has nice thick paper that is great for acrylic.
Content: This kit is super cute and was very well received by our teen artist. Pens work great and the included book has nice thick paper that is great for acrylic. The book included pages to test each of the colors to see how they look on paper next to each other which is neat. Paint came out of the markers smoothly and did not bleed. It dried rather quickly and created a very bright and vibrant image. We are very happy with the quality!

Sentence: On some of the colors you cannot see the numbers at all, so I abandoned the numbers entirely while swatching them.I absolutely love the little sketchbook that came with this set.
Content: The markers in this set are fantastic. They're highly pigmented, include rich and intense colors, with a good range for a set of 18. You do need to prime them prior to using, and make sure to shake them really well before each use. If you do that, you will not be disappointed in their performance.They are quite opaque, even the white. Again, if you don't shake them well enough, you won't get good coverage with them. The white marker rivals the opacity of the white Posca marker. Not completely 100% opaque, but pretty darn close. With a second coat, you get great coverage.The pens are a little spattery if you're not super careful with them. I'm guessing that this is due to the plastic nib. If you're very careful, you can sort of control that, though.I will say that I really dislike the numbering system. The numbers are sometimes impossible to read, and they seem to be backwards, so to read them correctly you'd have to read them by looking inside the cap. On some of the colors you cannot see the numbers at all, so I abandoned the numbers entirely while swatching them.I absolutely love the little sketchbook that came with this set. It has multiple colors of paper and it's nice, heavy paper, very cardstock-like and has the tiniest bit of tooth. The swatch template included is really creative, and I really appreciate that they provide both a black and white swatch page so you can see how each color performs on both dark and light surfaces (and the colors look VERY different on each).The ink dries pretty quickly with a single coat. With multiple coats (like if you need full coverage on dark paper) does take longer.Generally, these markers work great and I will be using them often.These markers would make a great gift for coloring enthusiasts or the artist in your life, whether they're a beginner or  more experienced.Overall, I highly recommend these markers!

Sentence: These markers are great!Love love LOVE the extra fine tips for doodling or adding details to coloring books or other art.
Content: These markers are great!Love love LOVE the extra fine tips for doodling or adding details to coloring books or other art. In comparison with the Grabie dual brush tip acrylic markers, these do have to be shaken and primed but they prime without too much effort. They come with a marker pad that includes both white and black swatch sheets, which I appreciate.Because they are extra fine tip markers, they are better for detail work than for covering large areas of color. I like using them over alcohol markers or the other, wider tip Grabie acrylic markers I mentioned above, but the mushroom doodle attached to this review was all done with these extra fine tip markers.The colors in this 18 marker set are absolutely beautiful but I do want to note that there’s not really a true red included. If that’s an issue for you, these markers are sold in larger sets.This set would be an easy five stars if Grabie would just label the markers with color names or codes. I understand that not labeling them probably lowers manufacturing costs but it also greatly impacts enjoyment when you have to keep markers in order at all times so you’ll know what each one looks like on the swatch sheet.Overall, this is a great set though and I love Grabie art products.
